name: Farasan Islands Marine Reserve
blurb: Seagrass, dugongs and gazelles on coral islands in the southern Red Sea.

tip.title: Lose the seagrass
tip.text: Dugongs and green turtles graze seagrass. Set Seagrass to -100% and watch them, then the orcas that hunt young dugongs.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Strong sun in clear shallow water drives seagrass, mangroves and plankton, and warms the reef lagoons.
Rain is scarce in this arid region, so land plants on the islands depend on the little that falls.

nodes.name: Bacteria & scavenging invertebrates
nodes.desc: Break down dead seagrass, mangrove litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to sediment and water.
Underwater meadows in shallow lagoons. Seagrasses of the genus Halophila are a main food of dugongs.
A salt-tolerant tree recorded on the islands that holds shoreline sediment and shelters young marine life.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic drifting algae that base the open-water food chain, feeding copepods and small fish.

nodes.name: Acacia shrubs
nodes.desc: Thorny desert trees and shrubs. Wikipedia lists acacia leaves, flowers and fruit as the main food of Arabian gazelles.
Grazes seagrass, roots included. Wikipedia notes few natural predators, though orcas and sharks threaten young animals.
Adults mostly graze seagrass and algae. Islands in the area host nesting sea turtles, including endangered green turtles.

nodes.name: Copepods
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans in the plankton that graze phytoplankton and feed schooling fish.
Recorded in the waters off the islands. It hunts small fish and squid in groups.
Seabird recorded often near the islands. It plunge-dives for fish.
Sand-dwelling crabs that scavenge on beaches and take hatchling turtles, according to the turtle source.
A wading shorebird recorded on the islands that specialises in eating crabs.
A small scavenging vulture recorded on the islands. It feeds on carrion and scraps.
Fish are about 99 percent of its diet. It plunge-dives for live fish and is a well-recorded bird here.
An occasional visitor to the islands. It hunts dolphins and can take young dugongs.
